lms_catalog.title: FCSA: Architecting Interoperable Chiplet Systems
lms_catalog.short_description: Apply FCSA to chiplet system architecture, interfaces, boot, security, and evidence for interoperable integration.
lms_catalog.overview: Use Foundation Chiplet System Architecture (FCSA) 1.1.0 to review a chiplet system from architectural roles and interfaces to coordinated boot and maintained trust. A running accelerator integration case, narrated diagrams, knowledge checks, and practical workbook exercises connect the specification to supplier questions, integration evidence, and product requirements. Relevant 2026 OCP Global Summit presentations provide additional context.
lms_catalog.duration_note: Estimated learner time includes media, reading, workbook exercises, and knowledge checks; optional viewing of the full Summit recordings is excluded.

modules.summary: Define the system boundary and distinguish foundation, design, and profile requirements. Learn to interpret normative statements, compliance levels, and the evidence needed for a scoped architectural claim.
Compare Compute & Hub and Compute Tile systems. Use functionality, coherent caching, address translation, and required interfaces to classify chiplets and identify missing supplier evidence.

Trace functional requirements through protocol and transport mappings, compatible versions, and activity states. Compare boot-image loading models and distinguish sequence control, resource management, and security responsibilities.

Connect chiplet-local attestation evidence to system-level composition and policy decisions. Apply product-specific threat analysis and explain why updates, resets, debug changes, and recovery can require revalidation.

Assemble an integration evidence worksheet covering interfaces, boot, trust, lifecycle, and scalability. Examine transaction adaptation and combined snoop-filter demand, then distinguish published FCSA requirements from proposed Physical AI work.
